question: Should routine restart-required `config.patch` and `config.apply` writes in hot mode preserve their current direct restart, or intentionally adopt the file watcher’s warn-and-keep behavior?
rationale: Both behaviors are viable, but the PR changes an existing control-plane runtime contract and can leave successful RPC writes unapplied until a manual restart; source inspection cannot select that product/upgrade policy safely.

options.title: Preserve current RPC restart
options.body: Keep direct restart for routine restart-required RPC writes while applying the security-only hot-mode watcher carve-out.

options.title: Adopt watcher parity
options.body: Accept warn-and-keep for routine RPC writes, document the changed contract and provide an explicit operator recovery path.

recommendation.title: Preserve current RPC restart
recommendation.body: Keep direct restart for routine restart-required RPC writes while applying the security-only hot-mode watcher carve-out.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans core gateway reload semantics and public configuration documentation.
